title: Ferritin-Guided Iron Supplementation Enhances Post-Donation Recovery in Frequent Blood Donors - Hematology Advisor
abstract:
References: Karregat JHM, Meulenbeld A, Quee FA, et al. Ferritin-guided iron supplementation as an alternative or complement to prolonged blood donation intervals (FORTE): a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial. Lancet Haematol.
Alternate day or daily supplementation with 30 mg or 60 mg of iron significantly reduces iron deficiency and anemia in frequent blood donors with low ferritin, according to research published in The Lancet Haematology.
References: Karregat JHM, Meulenbeld A, Quee FA, et al. Ferritin-guided iron supplementation as an alternative or complement to prolonged blood donation intervals (FORTE): a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial. Lancet Haematol. 2025;12(9):e694-e704.
Ferritin-guided iron supplementation might…be a safe and effective alternative to protect donors from iron deficiency without the need for extended donation intervals.
This invaluable supply depends on the generosity of millions of blood donors,” the study authors explained in their report. “Regular whole-blood donation is associated with an elevated risk of developing iron deficiency (ferritin <15 μg/L) and low haemoglobin levels, potentially threatening donor health and donor availability.”
